adore: We adore perfection because we can't have it; it would disgust us if we had it. Perfect is inhuman, because human is imperfect.
adolescence: I don’t see a single concept of ‘national’ or ‘literature’. Rather, I’ve always been fascinated by language. I enjoy contemplating the great depth, complexity and delicacy of the layers of a culture in which a single language is in-built. I owe a great debt to poetry and fiction written in Korean, as I spent my adolescence immersed within these.
As quoted in "Interview with Han Kang" in The White Review (March 2016)

adoptive: "Why be happy when you could be normal?" Constance Winterson, adoptive mother of Jeanette Winterson.
adolescents: The tide of undecipherable signatures of mutinous adolescents which has washed over and bitten into the facades of monuments and the surface of public vehicles in the city where I live: graffiti as an assertion of disrespect, yes, but most of all simply an assertion... the powerless saying: I'm here, too.
"The Pleasure of the Image" (1985) from Writers on Artists edited by Daniel Halpern (1988), p. 98, North Point Press
